stem: Why is school information often requested at ADHD reviews when home behaviour seems straightforward?

options.text: School reports are only needed when a child has suspected hearing loss
ADHD assessment can be subjective, so reports from family and school both matter
Teacher input is mainly used to decide who can prescribe medication
School information is only relevant before age 4 years
Parent history is less useful than school testing and should usually be replaced

explanation: ADHD assessment can be subjective, so reports from family and school both matter. Symptoms may be seen differently across settings, and combining information from home and school helps build a more complete assessment.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 84

rationale: Family and school perspectives are both important because ADHD symptoms are context-dependent and assessment can be subjective.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because school reports are sought as part of ADHD assessment across settings, not only when hearing loss is suspected.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because ADHD assessment can be subjective, and information from both family and school helps capture symptoms across different settings.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because teacher input contributes to assessment and does not determine prescribing authority.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because school information remains relevant beyond early childhood whenever ADHD symptoms are being assessed.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because parent history remains important and is not replaced by school testing.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
